Soojin —

Thanks, attached is a small sample export (helios_traffic_sample.csv) — last 7 days of production traffic for our primary /generate endpoint plus a short notes block below. Quick answers inline:

- Typical sustained QPS: 12 qps overall
- Peak QPS observed (1-minute): 180 qps (burst events twice/week)
- Concurrency: about 150 concurrent sessions at peak; ~60 persistent sessions during normal hours
- Prompt tokens (p10/p50/p90): 40 / 120 / 640
- Response tokens (p10/p50/p90): 20 / 80 / 420
- Long-context usage: ~5% of calls use > 2k tokens (document retrieval flows)
- KV cache: we do server-side session affinity for ~30% of sessions (chat-like flows)
- Latency targets: customer-facing p95 <= 600ms, p99 <= 1200ms (we’d like p99 < 1s if possible)
- Growth: expect 2–3x traffic in 9 months after launch; new endpoints planned in Q4

Notes: sample includes hourly aggregates + a CSV of raw requests by timestamp. We’re open to a recommended safety margin — initial ask from procurement was to see a 30% buffer.

Samir (cc’d) will help loop in procurement for contracts once sizing looks reasonable.

—Ari

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing — traffic shape & safety margin Qs

Thanks for the fork. Initial read of Ari's numbers — here are early strawman notes (quick internal that we should refine before sending externally):

- Workload summary (from sample): sustained ~12 qps, peak short bursts to ~180 qps, p90 prompt 640 tokens, p90 response 420 tokens, ~5% long-context retrieval calls; session affinity ~30%.

Strawman capacity (1x + 30% buffer):
- Candidate GPU: A40-class 48GB (quantized LLMs) or 80GB A100 for long-context models.
- Estimated fleet: 6 x A40 (in steady configuration) to meet sustained throughput + ability to absorb short bursts with autoscale and queuing; with burst pods (2x smaller SKUs) to push short-term 180 qps spikes.
- If they rely on long-context flows (5% calls) and want <1s p99, consider mixing 2 x A100-80GB nodes to host retrieval-augmented sessions; these can be pinned to the traffic with affinity.

Notes / clarifying questions for Ari:
- KV cache hit rate: what is the cache hit rate on session-affine calls? If high (>60%), we can reduce GPU counts via prefix caching.
- Tokenization: confirm tokenizer (we assumed standard BPE comparable to our benchmark).
- Acceptable cold-start latencies for autoscale (how long can queued requests wait?)

Cost & rollout options:
- Ballpark committed monthly: $XXk–$YYk (I’ll refine once we choose SKUs and region).
- For 2x growth, plan to add 4 additional A40 nodes (or convert burst pods to permanent) and expand canary routing.

I’ll draft a one-slide summary and an assumptions table. Marissa — want me to include a small table of tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs safety margin)?

—Karthik
